name: Lucky Dumpling House
tagline: Hand-folded dumplings from a family recipe four generations old.
origin_story:
Mei and her mother opened Lucky Dumpling House in 2019 after years of selling dumplings out of their home kitchen to neighbors and friends. The recipe traces back to Mei's great-grandmother in Shandong province, who fed travelers from a roadside stall during the 1940s.

Every dumpling is still folded by hand each morning. Mei estimates she's pleated more than two million of them since opening. The restaurant employs six people, four of them family members, and donates leftover dumplings to a local shelter every Sunday.

My mother said if the dumplings ever taste like a factory made them, we should close," Mei says. "So we keep folding.""

name: Saigon Corner
tagline: A second-generation pho shop where the broth simmers for 18 hours.
origin_story:
Linh's parents arrived in Maryland in 1982 with very little besides a recipe for pho written on the back of a photograph. They opened the original Saigon Corner in 1991 in a strip mall that no longer exists. Linh took over in 2018 after her father's retirement.

The broth recipe hasn't changed in three decades. Linh tested updating it twice and reverted both times after her regulars staged what she calls a peaceful protest with chopsticks."

id: The walls hold photographs of every family who has worked there, including a wedding photo of her parents taken behind the counter in 1993."
name: Linh Nguyen
Binh's Books & Tea
tagline: A bookshop and tea bar specializing in Southeast Asian literature in translation.
origin_story:
Binh opened the shop in 2022 after a decade as a librarian. The collection focuses on contemporary fiction, poetry, and cookbooks from Vietnam, Thailand, Cambodia, Laos, and the Philippines — much of it hard to find anywhere else in the region.

The back of the shop has a small tea bar with seven rotating Southeast Asian teas. Binh hosts a monthly reading group and an annual Lunar New Year poetry night that has, somehow, never had an empty seat.

I wanted a place where the books I grew up wishing existed could finally sit on a shelf," Binh says."
